rv.q: Yet the production that opened on Wednesday night at the Theater warrants not only sighs of relief but also at least a few lusty cheers.
While no theatrical air ball, 'Lysistrata Jones' isn't a slam dunk, either.
The plot remains silly, the music humdrum and the characters trite.
The show scores on its own terms.
The derivative combines campy comedic antics with no stakes whatsoever, unless some joker has given you Athens U. in the March Madness pool.

Don't get me started. I missed the upbeat show with the repugnant concept last summer when the Transport Group had a successful run with it downtown in a hip church gym. Transferred now to Broadway, the thing proves to be as trivializing and demeaning as it sounded.
Apart from a few new jokes and some heightened production values, 'Lysistrata Jones' remains unchanged and is as sharp and sassy as ever.
But too much of the time, it plays like a slightly raunchier version of a Nickelodeon or Disney Channel sitcom, rife with predictable plotlines and broad cultural and racial stereotypes.
A spirit of rah-rah positive thinking infuses the evening: sometimes for good, as in the finale, but more often with disappointing results.
Beane is the author of such amusing, sophisticated comedies as 'The Little Dog Laughed' and 'As Bees in Honey Drown,' as well as the very funny book for the musical 'Sister Act.
